title: Adaptive Temperature Autotuner — personal scratchpad
body:
Purpose / one-liner:

Small, client/edge-side and proxy-capable autotuner for sampling temperature (and related sampling knobs) that adapts per-conversation and per-turn to improve perceived quality while respecting token budget + latency targets. Not a replacement for RLHF / preference training — tactical runtime control that nudges sampling distribution based on cheap signals.

Why this?
- Observed large variance in user satisfaction across identical prompts when temperature is static.
- Some customers want deterministic behaviour occasionally (low temp) and creativity for others (high temp) without manual routing to different model variants.
- We can get cost/latency wins by lowering sampling entropy when confusion / hallucination risk is low and ramping when user explicitly asks for novelty.

Design goals / constraints:
- Lightweight: config + tiny heuristics run in client/proxy; no heavy model in the loop.
- Explainable: decisions should be traceable in telemetry (why temp changed).
- Reversible / conservative: avoid flipping temp mid-stream unless explicit signal or clear metric.
- Compatible with Redwood runtime: should be implementable as a pre-ingress filter (client SDK) or an ingress middleware (proxy).

Signals we can use (cheap / available at call time):
- Prompt features: presence of code block, system instruction, explicit generation style tokens ("poem", "draft"), length of user input.
- Conversation history stats: repeated confirmations, user edits, user rating flags (if app surface provides).
- Runtime telemetry: recent token sampling entropy (approx), per-token latency, number of streaming reconnects, API error rates.
- Business constraints: remaining token budget for session or tenant, per-route SLA.

Heuristic examples:
- If prompt contains "exactly", "precise", or code fences -> temp = 0.0..0.2 (deterministic mode).
- If user previously rated last result "creative" or used explicit "regenerate with more creative" intent -> increase temp +0.2 up to 0.9 with decay window.
- If session token budget low (< threshold) -> scale temp down proportional to remaining budget to reduce sampling entropy and average tokens per reply.
- If recent responses show high prefix-repeat (indicative of repetition/hallucination), reduce temp and optionally trigger higher-beam-like sampling (nucleus p adjust).

API / config sketch (flat JSON-like shape for client SDK):

{
  "autotune_enabled": true,
  "mode": "hybrid",               // static | hybrid | adaptive-only
  "base_temperature": 0.7,
  "min_temperature": 0.0,
  "max_temperature": 1.0,
  "signals": {
    "prompt_keywords": ["poem","draft","code","precise","citation"],
    "budget_policy": {"enabled": true, "min_tokens_left": 200, "scale_factor": 0.5},
    "user_feedback_weight": 0.6,
    "conversation_entropy_window": 5
  },
  "decay_seconds": 3600,           // how fast temporary boosts decay per session
  "telemetry_tags": ["autotune.v1", "source:client-sdk"]
}

Notes:
- "mode" semantics: 
  - static: ignore signals, use base_temperature
  - hybrid: apply only high-confidence rules (keywords, budget)
  - adaptive-only: use full heuristics including learned thresholds from telemetry

Server-side support / optional endpoints:
- /autotune/probe (POST): client sends summarized signal blob; server returns suggested temp + rationale. Useful for heavy heuristics or future learned policy.
- /autotune/report (POST): telemetry sink: what temp was chosen, signals, outcome metrics (user rating, regen).

Telemetry / metrics to capture (important for rollback & evaluation):
- chosen_temperature (per call)
- signal_snapshot: flattened short list (e.g., "has_code=true,user_feedback=+1")
- outcome_ballot: user action (like, regen, flag) and approximate answer length
- token_consumption_delta vs baseline (if baseline runs available)
- perceived-latency-impact (if any)

Offline evaluation plan:
1) A/B: baseline fixed-temp (0.7) vs adaptive mode on safe subset of traffic (low risk endpoints).
2) Collect metrics for: user-initiated regenerates, flags, average tokens/response, downstream session retention.
3) Evaluate on prompt-suites that measure hallucination rate (QA dataset), creativity metrics (diversity), and compliance-sensitive prompts.
4) Manual pass: sample hand-inspected outputs for safety/regression.

Failure modes / risks:
- Lowering temperature reduces hallucination but can also remove necessary diversity (user unhappy).
- Signal manipulation: malicious prompt text could force deterministic outputs for model extraction attempts. Need heuristics to prevent adversarial keyword exploitation.
- Oscillation: rapid toggles between high/low temp causing inconsistent UX. Use hysteresis and decay windows.
- Auditability: customers want to know when model behaviour changed; must log decisions and make auditable.

Open questions / research directions:
- Can we compute a cheap proxy for model uncertainty client-side? (e.g., n-gram surprise, token-level repetition)
- How to combine budget-aware decisions with user-intent signals gracefully? Priority rules vs scoring?
- Should we expose a discrete safety override that always enforces deterministic mode for compliance routes?
- Is learned policy (server-side) worth the privacy tradeoffs vs local heuristics?

Rollout strategy (suggested):
- Canary 1: internal / staging routes w/ telemetry-only (no changes to temp) for 2 weeks.
- Canary 2: hybrid mode on <1% low-risk production routes + telemetry.
- Canary 3: expand to 5-10% with auto rollback triggers (regens up x%, user flags up y%).

Implementation TODOs (short):
- [ ] implement local heuristics library in JS + Go (shared logic)
- [ ] add telemetry tags and schema in Redwood tracing
- [ ] create probe endpoint proto & rate limits
- [ ] experiment harness: replay previous sessions and simulate budget constraints
- [ ] safety review for keyword heuristics and adversarial cases

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider using simple bandit policy per-session: keep two temps A/B and nudge towards better-performing one with Thompson sampling on user-feedback proxy. Keeps logic simple and interpretable.
- Make the autotuner state optional and removable by app developer; default should be off.
- Add an opt-in consent flag for telemetry attribution when traffic contains PII-sensitive prompts.

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally informal — aim to turn into a short RFC once experiments produce clear wins.
